subject: mathematics
question_text: In a △ABC, prove that cot A + cot B + cot C = (a² + b² + c²)/(4Δ).

mark_split.label: Use the cosine rule and the area

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.75 — SAQ chapter 13 Properties of Triangles, answer 81, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: TS 15 · AP 16. The whole-angle partner of answer 80. Here the route is through the cosine rule and the area formula rather than a standard cotangent result. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: the same book prints 1+1+1+1 for the 4-mark answers 58 and 59 on book p.63 and 1+2+1 for answer 61 on p.64, so both shapes used in this unit are the book's own. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q17 is the Properties of Triangles slot. Together with Q24 (LAQ) this unit holds TWO slots — one of only two units to do so, Matrices being the other.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

steps.label: Use the cosine rule and the area
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Write cot as cos/sin, put the cosine rule on top, and note that 2bc sinA is 4Δ — because Δ = ½ bc sinA.
lines: L.H.S = cotA + cotB + cotC = cosA/sinA + cosB/sinB + cosC/sinC
Now Δ = ½ bc sinA ⇒ 2bc sinA = 4Δ, and similarly for the others

recall.must_convey: That cot = cos/sin, the cosine rule is used on each numerator, and 2bc sinA = 4Δ.
accept: write cot as cos over sin then use the cosine rule on top and delta equals half b c sin A underneath
two b c sin A is four delta
cosine rule and area formula vaadali, four delta vasthundi
convert every denominator to four delta

steps.why: Δ = ½ bc sinA gives 2bc sinA = 4Δ — so every one of the three denominators becomes the same thing, which is what lets the numerators simply add.
common_mistakes: Using the sine rule where the area formula is needed.

steps.label: Add and conclude
steps.margin_note: The other half. With a common denominator of 4Δ, the three numerators add — and every squared term survives exactly once.
lines: a²: −a² + a² + a² = a²  (and likewise for b², c²)

recall.must_convey: That the three numerators add over 4Δ and each squared term survives once, giving (a²+b²+c²)/(4Δ).
accept: add the three numerators over four delta and each square appears once giving a squared plus b squared plus c squared
minus a squared plus a squared plus a squared leaves one a squared
the answer is the sum of the squares over four delta
anni kalipithe a square plus b square plus c square by four delta
the numerators collapse to the sum of squares
heard_as: a squared plus b squared plus c squared

steps.why: Each squared term appears three times — twice positive, once negative — so exactly one of each survives. Tracking that is the whole of the last step.
common_mistakes: Cancelling all the squared terms to zero.
